name: Eyebrow microblading

angle.text: Users get it to fill thin or uneven brows with hair-like strokes, producing fuller, darker brows that last a long time. The visible result is the pigment itself. Case reports exist on side effects, and men weigh how natural it looks.

summary: Semi-permanent pigment strokes tattooed into the brows; popular for fuller brows, with case reports of infection and allergy.
note: Literature includes granuloma, allergy, cellulitis and mpox case reports.
currentQuick:
Microblading uses a handheld blade to deposit pigment in hair-like strokes in the brows. Results fade over one to two years and need touch-ups.
Men in forums discuss it as a way to get thicker, darker brows, with mixed opinions on how natural it looks.
How it works: Pigment, usually iron-oxide based, is placed in the superficial dermis, where it stays visible until it fades.
Risks and caveats: Case reports describe granulomas, sarcoidosis, allergic reactions, cellulitis and mpox transmission. Regulation varies by region.
deepLead:
Microblading is a semi-permanent cosmetic tattooing technique in which a technician uses a handheld tool with fine blades or needles to draw hair-like strokes of pigment into the upper dermis of the eyebrows. It is used to fill sparse, thin or uneven brows and to disguise brow loss.
Wikipedia reports results can last up to about two years, with a touch-up recommended around six weeks later and then every 12 to 18 months. Published clinical literature consists largely of reviews and case reports of complications, including granulomatous reactions, sarcoidosis, allergic contact dermatitis, cellulitis and a reported mpox transmission.
In looksmaxxing forums, microblading is discussed by men who want thicker, darker brows, with opinions that range from favourable to critical of how natural the results look.

name: Powder / ombre / nano brows

angle.text: Users choose these semi-permanent brow tattoos for a soft, shaded fill that looks like brow makeup, visible straight after the session. They are popular salon services with no dedicated studies.

summary: Machine-applied semi-permanent brow tattoo for a soft shaded fill; popular salon service with no dedicated studies.
note: Pigment migration, colour change and infection are documented risks of tattooing; regulation varies.
currentQuick:
Powder, ombre and nano brows are salon names for semi-permanent eyebrow tattoos applied with a machine to create a soft, shaded, make-up-like fill, as opposed to the hair-like strokes of microblading.
They are used to fill sparse or uneven brows. No published studies specific to these styles were found, so what is known comes from general information on cosmetic tattooing.
How it works: Pigment, commonly iron-oxide based, is deposited into the upper skin layers with fine needles. Because it sits relatively shallow, it fades over months to a couple of years, and touch-ups are typically recommended [1].
Risks and caveats: Reported risks include infection, reactions to pigment, granulomas, pigment migration and colour change. In the US there is no federal regulation or standard for testing the ink, and rules vary elsewhere.
deepLead:
Powder, ombre and nano brows are names used for semi-permanent cosmetic eyebrow tattooing in which pigment is deposited with a machine rather than drawn stroke by stroke by hand. Powder and ombre styles aim for a soft, shaded, make-up-like fill that is typically lighter at the front of the brow and darker toward the tail, while nano brows use very fine needles for a subtler result. These terms are trade and salon vocabulary rather than medical ones.
Related hand-applied microblading is described by Wikipedia as eyebrow tattooing in which individual hair-like strokes are made with a handheld tool, in contrast to the machine method used for most eyebrow tattoos . The same article notes that pigment placed in the upper dermis fades faster than in conventional tattoos, that touch-ups are commonly recommended, and that risks include pigment migration, colour change, infection and granulomas . No clinical studies specific to powder, ombre or nano techniques were found.

name: Henna brows

chain: Plant dye stains brow hair and skin
angle.text: Users get henna applied to darken and define their brows, with the stain visible immediately and lasting days to weeks. The result is a surface stain on hair and skin and is directly observable.

summary: Plant-dye stain on brow hair and skin that lasts days to weeks; the main documented hazard is adulterated 'black henna'.
note: Products containing PPD ('black henna') can cause severe allergic reactions; G6PD deficiency is a reported contraindication.
currentQuick:
Henna brows use a plant-based paste to stain the brow hairs and the skin beneath them, giving a darker, more filled-in look without a tattoo.
The stain is temporary. Skin stains typically fade within one to three weeks, and no dedicated clinical studies of the brow treatment were found.
How it works: Lawsone, the dye in henna, binds to keratin in hair and skin when the leaf paste is applied. It is released only after the leaves are dried, powdered and mixed [1].
Risks and caveats: Pure henna is reported to rarely cause reactions, but additives and PPD-containing 'black henna' can cause severe allergy and scarring. The FDA has not approved henna for direct skin use, and G6PD deficiency is a noted danger [1].
deepLead:
Henna brows are a salon service in which a paste made from henna, a plant dye, is applied to the eyebrow hairs and underlying skin to darken or define them. The staining agent in henna is lawsone, which is released when the dried leaves are powdered and made into a paste . Because the stain sits on the skin surface and hair, it is temporary.
Wikipedia reports that henna skin stains typically fade by exfoliation within one to three weeks, and that henna is also used as a temporary eyebrow tint . Pure henna rarely causes allergic problems, though additives in commercial pastes have been linked to reactions, and so-called black henna products may contain para-phenylenediamine (PPD), which can cause severe reactions . No clinical studies of henna eyebrow treatments were found.

name: Brow shaving / brow reshaping for tilt

angle.text: Looksmaxxers reshape or trim brows to change how angled the eye area looks, aiming for a positive tilt or 'hunter eyes' look. The change is cheap, reversible and visible right away. Its effect on perceived tilt has not been studied.

summary: Trimming or reshaping the brows to change how tilted the eye area looks; cheap and reversible, with no studies on its effect on perceived tilt.
note: Surgical brow shaping research exists, but none addresses shaving or trimming for tilt.
currentQuick:
Brow reshaping for tilt means trimming, shaving or styling the eyebrows so the eye area appears more upward-angled. It is a grooming technique discussed in looksmaxxing circles alongside canthal tilt.
No studies were found that test whether brow trimming changes perceived tilt. The published literature concerns surgical brow shaping and lifting.
How it works: Hair is removed or trimmed with tweezers, wax, thread, scissors or a razor to change the brow's outline, sometimes with makeup to redraw it [1]. Surgeons shape the brow by lifting different parts of it, emphasising the medial-lateral relationship [2].
Risks and caveats: Hair generally regrows, so grooming changes are temporary. Surgical options carry standard operative risks and are outside the scope of grooming.
deepLead:
Brow reshaping for tilt refers to trimming, shaving or otherwise altering the eyebrows to change how the eye area appears angled, a concern in looksmaxxing discussions of positive canthal tilt and the 'hunter eyes' look. In everyday grooming this is done by removing or trimming hair; Wikipedia lists tweezing, waxing, threading and trimming as common methods, and notes that some people shave the brows and draw them on .
Published research on the topic is surgical rather than cosmetic grooming. Plastic surgeons have described procedures that reshape brow position, including transcutaneous brow shaping and gliding brow lifts, in which the relationship between the medial and lateral portions of the brow is emphasised over overall height . No studies of brow shaving or trimming for perceived eye tilt were found.

name: Brow thread lift

angle.text: Users get threads placed to raise the tail of the brow without surgery, giving a lifted look that is visible after the procedure. It is offered as an alternative to surgical brow lifts. Evidence on how long it lasts is thin.

summary: Threads placed to hoist the brow tail without surgery; evidence is thin, with one trial on durability just registered.
note: No published trial results found; durability is the open question.
currentQuick:
A brow thread lift uses threads under the skin to raise the outer part of the eyebrow, offered as a less invasive alternative to a surgical brow lift.
Sources reviewed contain no completed trials. A registered study is planned to test how long the effect lasts.
How it works: Threads are anchored in the brow and forehead tissue to hold the brow tail higher. Surgical lifts instead reposition tissue through incisions, and botulinum toxin raises the brow by relaxing opposing muscles [1].
Risks and caveats: Specific complication rates for brow threads were not found. Brow lifts in general carry risks such as infection, bleeding and numbness [1].
deepLead:
A brow thread lift is a minimally invasive procedure in which threads are placed under the skin to suspend and raise the tail of the eyebrow. It is offered as an alternative to surgical brow lifts, which Wikipedia describes as procedures to raise drooping brows, with types including endoscopic, coronal and direct approaches, and non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin .
Published evidence is limited. One registered trial, not yet recruiting as of its listing, plans to examine whether upper blepharoplasty with ligament release improves the durability of thread-assisted brow suspension . No completed clinical studies were found in the material reviewed.

name: Orbital rim implants

chain: Implant adds bony support under eye
Hollow and tear trough fill out
angle.text: Hardmaxxing circles discuss silicone or porous implants along the lower orbital rim to build support under the eye and smooth hollows, a change that is visible once healed. It is promoted as more durable than fillers; published data is thin.

summary: Silicone or porous implants set along the lower orbital rim for under-eye bony support; popular in hardmaxxing talk, thin on published data.
note: Surgical; reported complications include eyelid malposition, infection, extrusion and nerve injury.
currentQuick:
Orbital rim implants are synthetic implants placed on the bony rim under the eye to reduce hollowing and support the lower lid, sometimes combined with cheek (malar) implants.
They are discussed in forums as a durable alternative to filler. Published data on cosmetic use are limited, and much of the satisfaction evidence comes from malar implants.
How it works: A silicone, porous polyethylene or similar implant, standard or custom-made from CT scans, is placed under the periosteum of the rim and secured, adding projection to the bony support [1].
Risks and caveats: Reported complications include lower eyelid malposition, infection, contour irregularities and implant extrusion, and rarely nerve injury or sinus fistula [1]. It is a surgical procedure with recovery of several weeks.
deepLead:
Infraorbital or orbital rim implants are alloplastic (synthetic) devices placed along the lower orbital rim to add bony support under the eye. Grokipedia describes them as typically made of medical-grade silicone, intended for tear trough hollows, rim recession and a negative orbital vector, and presented as a more durable alternative to fillers or fat grafting .
Published evidence is limited. Grokipedia states that large studies of infraorbital implants are scarce and cites satisfaction figures mainly from malar implant series . In looksmaxxing forums the implants are discussed, often alongside malar implants, as a hardmaxxing option for eye-area support, with debate over standard versus custom designs .

name: Infraorbital rim / zygomatic filler

chain: Filler added at under-eye rim and cheekbone
angle.text: Users get hyaluronic acid filler placed around the lower orbital rim and cheekbone to add support under the eyes and a more structured mid-face, visible after treatment. The result is temporary.

summary: Hyaluronic acid filler placed around the under-eye rim and cheekbone for support; temporary, with a delicate and risky injection area.
note: Rare vascular occlusion can cause skin necrosis or permanent vision loss; common effects are bruising and swelling.
currentQuick:
Infraorbital rim and zygomatic filler uses injectable gel, usually hyaluronic acid, to add volume under the eye and over the cheekbone for a more supported look.
Evidence consists of small pilot studies, anatomical studies and complication reviews; no large trials were found.
How it works: Filler is injected into the tissue around the orbital rim and cheek to add volume and projection. Researchers are studying depth, vessel locations and fat patterns to refine placement [3][5][6].
Risks and caveats: Common effects are bruising, swelling, blue-grey tint and contour irregularities [2]. Rarely, filler entering an artery can cause tissue death or permanent vision loss [1]. Fillers are regulated as medical devices in the US [1].
deepLead:
Infraorbital rim and zygomatic filler refers to injectable fillers, usually hyaluronic acid, placed around the lower orbital rim and cheekbone to add apparent support under the eye. Wikipedia describes injectable fillers as materials used to smooth wrinkles, restore volume and contour areas such as the cheeks . In appearance communities the aim is often described as building skeletal-looking support for a deeper-set, more supported eye region.
The infraorbital area is anatomically delicate. Reviews list bruising, malar oedema, blue-grey discolouration and contour irregularities as common complications, with uncommon serious events . Small pilot and cadaver studies have examined placement and behaviour of hyaluronic acid in the region .

name: Fat grafting (lower eyelid / tear trough)

chain: Own fat moved into tear trough
angle.text: Patients use it to soften hollow under-eye areas with their own fat, giving a visibly smoother transition from lid to cheek. Evidence comes mostly from case series.

summary: Moving your own fat into the under-eye hollow to soften the tear trough: a real surgical option backed mostly by case series, with lumps and irregularities among the reported complications.
note: Evidence is mainly case reports and retrospective series; contour irregularities and graft resorption are documented.
currentQuick:
Fat grafting for the lower eyelid takes a small amount of a person's own fat from another body area, processes it, and injects it into the hollow between the lower lid and cheek (the tear trough) to even out the contour. Forum users discuss it as a longer-lasting alternative to hyaluronic acid filler for under-eye hollows.
A systematic review of eyelid fat grafting found the literature consisted mostly of case reports and retrospective case series, so the quality of evidence is limited.
How it works: Harvested fat is injected as volume under the thin eyelid skin, filling the depression and smoothing the lid-cheek transition. Proponents also say the transferred tissue may improve skin quality, which is a claim researchers are still studying.
Risks and caveats: Reported problems with fat grafting in general include swelling, bruising, infection, lumpy or uneven contours, partial reabsorption of the fat and fat necrosis. The thin eyelid skin makes irregularities more visible. It is an operation performed by surgeons, and results can shift with major weight change.
deepLead:
Fat grafting of the lower eyelid and tear trough, also called periorbital lipofilling or autologous fat transfer, is a surgical procedure in which a patient's own fat is harvested from another part of the body, processed and injected into the hollow beneath the lower eyelid to restore volume and smooth the transition to the cheek .
It is used for people who are bothered by a pronounced tear trough, hollow under-eye contour or volume loss, and is sometimes combined with lower blepharoplasty . In looksmaxxing communities it appears in discussions of hardmaxxing options for the eye area, alongside fillers and eyelid surgery .
A systematic review of eyelid fat grafting noted that the published literature consisted mostly of case reports and retrospective case series, with no earlier study assessing overall complication or satisfaction rates across techniques . The evidence base is therefore described as limited.

name: Transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty

angle.text: Users get it to remove or reposition under-eye fat for a flatter, less puffy lower lid, with no external scar. The result is the visible change itself once swelling settles.

summary: Lower-eyelid surgery through an incision inside the lid, so there is no outer scar, used to remove or reposition under-eye fat bags.
note: Best suited to fat bags without much excess skin; skin laxity may need a separate procedure.
currentQuick:
In transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty the surgeon works through a cut on the inner surface of the lower eyelid, which leaves no visible external scar. It is used to remove or move the fat that bulges as under-eye bags and to smooth the lid-cheek transition.
It is an established surgical technique described in plastic-surgery literature, including combinations with fat grafting and other steps. Published support comes largely from surgeon case series rather than randomized trials.
How it works: Orbital fat is either removed or repositioned along the infraorbital rim to fill the tear trough hollow. Because there is no skin incision, it is generally described as suitable when there is little or no excess skin.
Risks and caveats: Swelling and bruising are common and usually settle over several weeks. Eyelid malposition is a recognized complication of lower blepharoplasty in general, and surgeons sometimes add a canthopexy or canthoplasty to reduce that risk. It is a surgical procedure done under anesthesia by qualified surgeons.
deepLead:
Transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty is a form of lower-eyelid surgery in which the incision is made on the inner surface of the eyelid, leaving no external scar . It is used to remove or reposition the orbital fat that produces under-eye bags and tear trough hollowing.
Surgical descriptions state that it suits patients with minimal or no excess skin, whereas a transcutaneous incision just below the lashes is typically used when significant skin laxity needs to be addressed . Where skin laxity coexists, an additional procedure may be needed .
In the plastic-surgery literature the technique is described alone and in combination with fat grafting, including stromal vascular fraction gel, and with other steps tailored to specific lower-eyelid deformity types .

name: Plasma pen blepharoplasty

angle.text: It is promoted in DIY and salon circles as a non-surgical way to tighten loose eyelid skin for a better eye area, with cheap home devices also discussed. Almost no published clinical research backs the claim.

summary: A handheld plasma device used on eyelid skin to tighten it without surgery; popular in DIY and salon circles, with almost no published clinical research behind it.
note: No clinical studies found; scarring around the eye is a concern raised for the procedure.
currentQuick:
Plasma pen blepharoplasty is the use of a handheld plasma device to create tiny points of controlled skin injury on or around the eyelids, with the aim of tightening loose skin without cutting. It is marketed as a non-surgical alternative to eyelid surgery.
On looksmax.org one poster describes devices selling for roughly 40 to 60 dollars and clinic treatments at 400 to 1,900 dollars, and recommends the eyelids, nasal folds, forehead and neck as target areas. No clinical studies of the technique were found in the sources reviewed.
How it works: Proponents say the pen's energy causes controlled damage that prompts the skin to contract and rebuild collagen, which fibroblasts produce. This mechanism has not been tested in published eyelid trials in the sources reviewed.
Risks and caveats: The skin of the eyelid is very thin and close to the eye, and scarring is a concern commonly raised about plasma treatments in this area. No safety data for eyelid use were found in the sources reviewed. Forum posts describe both clinic treatment and the purchase of inexpensive devices.
deepLead:
Plasma pen blepharoplasty, also called plasma fibroblasting eyelid lift, is a non-surgical cosmetic procedure that uses a handheld plasma device to tighten loose or wrinkled eyelid skin. It is promoted as an alternative to surgical blepharoplasty.
On looksmax.org a poster describes the plasma pen as a device that simulates and rejuvenates sagging, wrinkled and dull skin, with the eyelids named as one of the most common treatment sites, along with the nasal fold area, forehead and neck .
No clinical studies of plasma pen use on the eyelids were found in the sources reviewed.

name: Polynucleotide eye filler

angle.text: Users get polynucleotide injections around the eyes for thin, crepey lower-lid skin, aiming for better-quality, fresher skin. Very little published evidence exists for this periorbital use.

summary: Polynucleotide injections around the eyes for thin, crepey lower-lid skin; very little published evidence turned up for the periorbital use.
note: Thin source base; no clinical studies of the eye-area use were found.
currentQuick:
Polynucleotide eye filler refers to injections of polynucleotide-based products into the thin skin around the eyes. The intent is to improve skin quality in the periorbital area rather than to add large volume.
Very little documentation was found for this use. A registered observational study of a periorbital rejuvenation procedure (n=29) exists, but its listing does not specify the product, so no studies were found for polynucleotide eye treatment specifically.
How it works: Proponents of polynucleotide injectables describe them as stimulating skin repair and hydration. No published eyelid-specific mechanism data were found in the sources reviewed.
Risks and caveats: Injections near the eye carry the general risks of periorbital injectables, including bruising, swelling and lumpiness, and the thin skin shows irregularities. No specific safety data for this use were found in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Polynucleotide eye filler is a name for injections of polynucleotide-based products into the thin skin of the lower eyelid and surrounding area, intended to improve the quality of periorbital skin.
The sources reviewed contain almost no published evidence on this use. One registered prospective, non-interventional study of a periorbital rejuvenation procedure (n=29, completed 2025) lists glabellar lines, midface volume deficiency and periorbital wrinkling as conditions, but the listing does not identify the product used .

name: Eyelid RF/laser tightening

chain: Laser or RF heats eyelid skin
angle.text: Users get fractional laser or radiofrequency treatment to firm lax eyelid skin and reduce fine lines without surgery. Small studies show modest improvement; heavy laxity is usually treated surgically.

summary: Fractional lasers (and radiofrequency devices) used to tighten loose eyelid skin without surgery; small studies show modest improvement, while heavy laxity is usually treated surgically.
note: Evidence is small prospective series; radiofrequency specifically was not covered by the studies found.
currentQuick:
Eyelid tightening with lasers or radiofrequency uses controlled heat to make loose or crepey eyelid skin firmer, as a non-surgical alternative to blepharoplasty. Fractional lasers are the best documented of these in the sources found.
Published work includes a prospective single-blinded study of ablative fractional CO2 laser on lower-eyelid laxity in 25 subjects, reports of non-ablative fractional resurfacing improving eyelid tightening and aperture, and a registered trial comparing fractional laser and ultrasound for periorbital wrinkles. These are small studies.
How it works: Fractional lasers create microscopic zones of thermal injury in the skin, which then heals with remodeling. The tightening is attributed to this wound-healing response.
Risks and caveats: Treating skin this close to the eye requires eye protection and expertise. Laser resurfacing carries general risks such as redness, swelling and pigment change. Marked eyelid laxity from tendon looseness is managed surgically, for example with a tarsal strip procedure, rather than by skin tightening.
deepLead:
Eyelid RF/laser tightening refers to non-surgical treatments that use laser or radiofrequency energy to firm lax eyelid skin and reduce fine lines, as an alternative to surgical blepharoplasty.
The published evidence found concerns mainly fractional lasers. A prospective, single-blinded study of ablative fractional carbon-dioxide laser in 25 subjects evaluated eyelid tightening with a series of two to three sessions . Other reports describe tightening and improved eyelid aperture after non-ablative fractional resurfacing and a niche role for fractional CO2 laser in eyelid skin tightening .
Radiofrequency-specific studies of eyelid tightening were not among the sources reviewed.

name: Vitamin K eye cream

angle.text: It is marketed for dark circles with a vascular component, where users hope to fade the bluish look under the eyes. The sources reviewed contain no clinical studies of it for this use.

summary: Topical vitamin K marketed for under-eye dark circles said to have a blood-vessel component; the sources reviewed contain no clinical studies of it.
note: No clinical studies found; effect on dark circles is unproven in the sources reviewed.
currentQuick:
Vitamin K eye cream is a cosmetic product applied under the eyes and marketed for dark circles with a vascular or bruise-like component. Vitamin K is a fat-soluble vitamin best known for its role in blood clotting.
No clinical studies of topical vitamin K for dark circles were found in the sources reviewed, so claims about its effect on under-eye darkness remain untested here.
How it works: Vitamin K is a cofactor for an enzyme that modifies clotting proteins, which is how it supports blood coagulation. Proponents of the cream link that clotting role to reducing blood pooling under the eyes; this link has not been tested in studies found for this entry.
Risks and caveats: Reference material on vitamin K notes that no toxicity is known from high oral intakes of K1 or K2, while intravenous injection can cause severe reactions. Those findings concern oral and injected forms, not creams. Dark circles have many causes, including anatomy, pigmentation, allergies and thin skin.
deepLead:
Vitamin K eye cream is a topical cosmetic product containing vitamin K, applied under the eyes and marketed for dark circles that are thought to have a vascular component, meaning visible blood vessels or pooled blood beneath thin skin.
Vitamin K is a group of fat-soluble vitamins: K1 (phylloquinone) from plants and K2 (menaquinones) from animal and fermented foods, with a role as a cofactor for the carboxylation of clotting factors .
Periorbital dark circles are attributed to several causes including anatomy, allergies and eye rubbing, medications, thin skin and increased pigmentation . No clinical studies of topical vitamin K for this condition were found in the sources reviewed.

name: Dermal rollers / microneedling eyes

angle.text: Users needle the skin around the eyes hoping to thicken it and soften dark circles. Microneedling has some evidence for scars, but little is specific to the eye area.

summary: Needling the thin skin around the eyes, claimed to thicken it and soften circles; microneedling has some evidence for scars, little specific to eyes.
note: Non-sterile or non-medical settings have been linked to infection warnings; eye-area skin is delicate.
currentQuick:
Dermal rollers and similar microneedling tools puncture the skin repeatedly with fine needles. Looksmaxxing communities discuss using them around the eyes to thicken thin skin and reduce a tired look.
Microneedling, or collagen induction therapy, has been studied mainly for acne scars, wrinkles and hair loss. Sources reviewed for this entry do not include trials of it specifically for the under-eye or eyelid area.
How it works: The needles create many tiny punctures, which proponents say trigger the skin's wound-healing response and collagen production. Wikipedia describes the procedure as repeatedly puncturing skin with tiny sterile needles.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia notes safety concerns about use in non-medical settings where staff lack infection-control training, citing a 2018 New Mexico health warning and a 2024 CDC announcement of HIV diagnoses in three women after microneedling with platelet-rich plasma at an unlicensed spa. The periorbital skin is delicate and close to the eye.
deepLead:
Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, skin needling or dermarolling, is a cosmetic procedure that repeatedly punctures the skin with tiny sterile needles. Handheld rollers and stamping devices are used by clinicians, and rollers are also sold for home use.
In looksmaxxing circles, needling the periorbital skin is discussed as a way to thicken thin under-eye skin and improve its appearance. No trial reviewed for this entry examined microneedling specifically for the eye area.
The best-studied uses of microneedling are acne and other scars, and it has been combined with minoxidil for hair loss in a 2013 pilot study.

name: Bates method eye exercises

angle.text: Promoted since the early 1900s as a way to improve eyesight without glasses, so some users hope to look without lenses. Reviews find no objective gain in eyesight, so its appearance link rests on belief.

summary: Early-20th-century relaxation and eye-movement routines promoted to improve vision; reviews find no objective gain in eyesight.
note: Some variants involve looking toward the sun; eye-care bodies warn of retinal and eyelid risks, and reliance on the method in place of corrective lenses has been criticised for safety reasons.
currentQuick:
The Bates method is a set of eye relaxation and eye-movement exercises devised by the New York eye physician William Horatio Bates (1860-1931). It is promoted as a way to improve eyesight without glasses. In looksmaxxing circles it appears in the fringe category, where some people say eye exercises can change how the eyes look or function.
Bates held that focusing errors come from mental strain on the muscles around the eyeball, and that relaxation could reverse them. Mainstream ophthalmology and optometry reject that explanation of how the eye focuses, and published reviews have not found that eye exercises objectively improve visual acuity.
How it works: Bates proposed that the external muscles of the eyeball, not the lens, change the eye's shape to focus, and that tension from mental strain causes myopia and other conditions. His techniques include palming (covering closed eyes with the palms), visualising dark objects, shifting and swinging the gaze, and sunning (exposing the eyes or closed lids to sunlight). Vision scientists attribute focusing to the ciliary muscle and lens, and explain apparent improvements as adaptation to blur or better interpretation of blurry images.
Risks and caveats: Reviews by ophthalmology bodies have found no objective improvement in eyesight from eye exercises. Critics have raised safety concerns, including driving or working without needed lenses, delaying treatment of conditions such as glaucoma or childhood amblyopia, and retinal or skin damage from looking toward the sun. The method is not a regulated medical treatment, and marketers of some Bates-derived programmes have faced legal action.
deepLead:
The Bates method is a system of eye relaxation and eye-movement exercises developed by the American eye physician William Horatio Bates (1860-1931) and promoted as a way to improve eyesight without corrective lenses. Bates published his main statement of the method in 1920 in a book titled The Cure of Imperfect Sight by Treatment Without Glasses, also issued as Perfect Sight Without Glasses.
Bates held that the muscles surrounding the eyeball change its shape to focus, that refractive errors and several other eye conditions arise from mental strain on those muscles, and that relaxation can relieve them. Mainstream eye care holds a different account of focusing, in which the ciliary muscle changes the shape of the lens. A 2013 paper in Ophthalmic and Physiological Optics discussed how the Bates method and other proposed myopia cures are claimed to work and why people report benefits.
A 2004 review by the American Academy of Ophthalmology found no evidence that eye exercises objectively improve eyesight, and a 2005 review of 43 studies from Christchurch Hospital reached a similar conclusion for visual acuity, according to Wikipedia. In looksmaxxing communities the method is sometimes mentioned alongside other fringe suggestions that eye exercises can alter eye function or appearance.

name: Hair bangs / frame hairstyle for eyes

angle.text: Users style bangs or face-framing hair to draw attention to the eyes and brow area and to shape the upper face, a visible change from the haircut itself. The claims about eye emphasis have little formal research.

summary: Fringe and face-framing hair used to draw attention to the eyes and brow area; a styling choice with little formal research behind the claims.
note: Evidence is limited to a cosmetology paper pairing hairlines with fringe styles.
currentQuick:
Bangs (fringe in British usage) are hair that falls over the front hairline to cover the forehead, usually just above the eyebrows. In looksmaxxing discussions, bangs and face-framing styles are said to focus attention on the eye and brow area and to alter the apparent forehead and face shape.
Bangs have a long history across cultures and fashions. Formal research on their effect on eye attractiveness is sparse.
How it works: Hair covering the forehead changes the visible hairline and frames the upper face. Proponents say this shifts attention to the eyes and shortens a long forehead. A 2022 cosmetology paper cited by Wikipedia paired five hairline shapes with fringe styles.
Risks and caveats: Styling carries no significant health risks. Practitioners note that bangs need regular trimming and styling.
deepLead:
Bangs, called fringe in British, Australian and New Zealand English, are strands of hair that fall over the front hairline to cover the forehead, usually just above the eyebrows. Their length and shape vary, and modern Western cuts are usually straight, though arc-shaped and ragged versions exist.
In looksmaxxing discussions, bangs and other framing hairstyles are described as a way to draw attention to the eyes and brow area. No published study reviewed for this entry tests that claim directly. A 2022 paper by Park and Jang in the International Journal of Advanced Culture Technology classified five hairline shapes and paired each with a fringe style using wig prototypes, and presents the pairings as cosmetology educational resources.

name: Eye whitening and brightening

angle.text: Looksmax.org posters argue white, bright sclera improves eye appearance through contrast, especially for brown eyes, and ask about eye drops. Little research targets this goal.

summary: Efforts to make the whites of the eyes look whiter and brighter, discussed for contrast and a fresher look; little research targets this goal.
note: Eye drops marketed for redness are a medical product category; users report trying them, and no study reviewed here tests them for appearance.
currentQuick:
Eye whitening and brightening refers to making the sclera (the white of the eye) look whiter and less red so the eyes appear fresher and higher in contrast. Users on looksmax.org describe white sclera and bright eyes as important for every eye colour because of contrast.
The sources found for this entry are thin. Published research reviewed is not about cosmetic eye whitening, so the article is short.
How it works: Proponents talk about reducing redness and the contrast between iris and sclera, and mention using eye drops. No studies reviewed examine how such methods affect perceived attractiveness.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia's eye drop article does not cover redness-relieving drops in depth; it says alpha agonist drops used for glaucoma have a higher likelihood of allergic reaction and list burning, stinging and other side effects. Persistent redness is commonly a reason for medical review.
deepLead:
Eye whitening and brightening is a looksmaxxing topic concerned with how white and clear the sclera looks and how bright the eyes appear. On looksmax.org, one user argued that sclera whiteness and brightness matter for every eye colour because of contrast, and said it is especially important for brown eyes; he asked others for ways to whiten the sclera and mentioned eye drops.
No studies reviewed for this entry test cosmetic eye whitening or its effect on attractiveness, so the evidence is untested. General eye-drop information on Wikipedia notes that alpha agonist drops, a class used for glaucoma, are more likely to cause allergic reactions, and that the article does not discuss redness-relieving vasoconstrictor products in depth.

name: Non-surgical rhinoplasty (liquid nose job)

angle.text: Users get filler injected to smooth a bridge bump, lift the tip or add projection without surgery, with the change visible immediately. Results are temporary.

summary: Injectable filler used to smooth a bump, lift the tip or add projection without surgery; results are temporary and rare vascular complications can be severe.
note: Case reports and reviews describe rare but serious vascular complications, including skin necrosis and vision loss, because of the nose's blood supply.
currentQuick:
Non-surgical rhinoplasty, often called a liquid nose job, uses injectable filler to alter the nose's profile without cutting. Practitioners use it to fill depressions, camouflage a dorsal hump, raise the tip angle, or add projection.
It appeals to people who want a change without surgery or recovery. Results from hyaluronic acid fillers are temporary, and the technique can only add volume; it does not reduce nose size.
How it works: A filler, most commonly a hyaluronic acid gel, is placed in selected points of the nose to change contour by adding volume and creating optical straightening. Hyaluronic acid can be broken down by the enzyme hyaluronidase, which is used in practice to address complications.
Risks and caveats: The nose's vessels connect with the ophthalmic artery, so accidental intravascular injection can cause skin ischaemia and, rarely, vision loss. Reviews and case series emphasise anatomical knowledge and safety technique. Other reported effects include swelling, bruising, asymmetry and granulomas. Regulatory approval of fillers varies by product and use.
deepLead:
Non-surgical rhinoplasty, also called liquid rhinoplasty, is a cosmetic procedure that reshapes the nose with injectable filler instead of surgery. Wikipedia describes it as using fillers such as collagen or hyaluronic acid to fill depressed areas, lift the angle of the tip or smooth bumps on the bridge, without changing the size of the nose.
The technique is described in the plastic-surgery literature as increasingly popular, and has been studied mainly in retrospective series and reviews, such as a single-centre retrospective analysis of a standardised five-point technique and a case series of 511 procedures over 16 years. The nose's vascular anatomy, including connections to the ophthalmic artery, makes accidental intra-arterial injection a recognised hazard, and papers have reported vision loss and skin ischaemia and treatment with high-dose hyaluronidase.
In looksmaxxing culture it is classed with hardmaxxing procedures as a reversible, lower-commitment alternative to surgical rhinoplasty.

name: Septoplasty

chain: Airway opens and nose aligns better
angle.text: Septoplasty is functional surgery for breathing, but people discuss it because it can make small cosmetic changes such as to the tip, and is often combined with rhinoplasty. Alone it may not straighten a crooked-looking nose.

summary: Functional surgery that straightens a deviated nasal septum to improve breathing; it is not a cosmetic nose reshaping, though the two are often combined.
note: Evidence supports symptom relief for obstruction; it is a breathing operation and is distinguished from rhinoplasty, which changes external appearance.
currentQuick:
Septoplasty is an operation that straightens the nasal septum, the wall of cartilage and bone between the two nostrils, when it is bent enough to block airflow. It is done through the nostrils, usually as an outpatient procedure.
It is primarily a functional surgery. In looksmaxxing forums it comes up because people with a crooked septum ask whether it will change how the nose looks, or whether it should be combined with rhinoplasty or jaw surgery.
How it works: The surgeon makes an incision in the lining of the septum, then removes or repositions deviated bone and cartilage while keeping enough for support. Splints, sutures or grafts may be used afterward. Because the incisions are inside the nose, there is generally no external scar, and the external shape is not the goal.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks include bleeding, septal perforation, septal haematoma, reduced sense of smell, temporary numbness of the front upper teeth, and, less often, a dropped nasal tip or saddle deformity from over-resection. Symptoms can persist or recur in some patients. Procedures on the turbinates carry their own discussed risks, such as empty nose syndrome.
deepLead:
Septoplasty is a surgical procedure that straightens a deviated nasal septum, the partition between the two nasal cavities, to relieve obstruction. It is also called septal reconstruction or submucous septal resection. It is performed through the nostrils, under local or general anaesthesia, and most operations take about an hour or less according to Wikipedia.
Its main indications are nasal obstruction, recurrent nosebleeds from a septal spur, and associated rhinitis or sinus problems. A multicentre prospective study of adults with septal deviation and symptomatic obstruction, the NOSE study, found improved disease-specific quality of life after septoplasty. A 2023 randomised trial published in the BMJ found greater improvement in symptoms at six months after septoplasty than with nasal sprays alone.
Septoplasty is distinct from rhinoplasty, which reshapes the external nose, although the two are often performed together as septorhinoplasty. In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed mainly as a breathing operation that some users ask about in relation to nose appearance, rhinoplasty and orthognathic surgery.

name: Septorhinoplasty

angle.text: Users have septum and outer-nose surgery together to fix breathing and reshape a crooked or unwanted nose, the visible result being the new nose shape. The evidence base is mostly surgical case series.

summary: Combined surgery on the nasal septum and the outer nose, done for breathing and shape together; the evidence base is mostly surgical case series, with recovery details well documented.
note: Surgical procedure under anaesthesia; swelling and tip position can take months to a year to settle, and revision surgery is a documented possibility.
currentQuick:
Septorhinoplasty combines septoplasty (straightening the cartilage and bone wall inside the nose) with rhinoplasty (reshaping the outside of the nose). It is performed when a person has both a breathing problem from a deviated septum and a wish to change nasal appearance, such as a crooked bridge after a past injury.
On looksmaxxing forums it appears in threads where members ask whether they need a plain rhinoplasty or the combined operation, and in recovery threads about swelling and tip position. Published research on it is largely surgical series and trials of peri-operative care rather than comparisons of cosmetic outcomes.
How it works: The surgeon works on the septum to correct deviation and on the nasal cartilages and bones to alter the external shape, using an open or closed approach. Cartilage from the septum is often reused as graft material, and the nasal bones may be repositioned.
Risks and caveats: Documented issues include bruising and swelling, persisting obstruction (sometimes linked to enlarged turbinates), the need for revision surgery, and anaesthesia-related effects such as sore throat. It is a prescription-level surgical procedure performed by licensed surgeons; outcomes vary by surgeon and anatomy.
deepLead:
Septorhinoplasty is an operation that combines septoplasty, which corrects a deviated nasal septum, with rhinoplasty, which reshapes the external nose. It is used when a patient has both an obstructed airway and an aesthetic concern, for example a crooked nose following trauma. Surgeons describe it as a common functional-aesthetic procedure, and trials registered in several countries study its recovery, pain control and outcomes.
The published evidence mostly consists of surgical technique reports, retrospective reviews and randomised trials of adjuncts such as tranexamic acid, corticosteroids, analgesia and anaesthetic methods, rather than head-to-head tests of aesthetic results. A review of septal surgery noted that, although its benefit seems intuitive, relatively few papers had confirmed it when the review was written.
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed mainly by people deciding between a rhinoplasty alone and the combined operation, and by people describing post-operative swelling and tip rotation.
